statement: Two triangular metal brackets are congruent. Triangle $PQR$ is congruent to triangle $XYZ$, with $P$, $Q$ and $R$ corresponding to $X$, $Y$ and $Z$. On the brackets, $PQ = 3t + 4$, $XY = 5t - 6$ and $YZ = 2t + 7$, all in centimeters. What is the length of $\overline{QR}$, in centimeters?

choices.misconception: I solved $3t + 4 = 5t - 6$ to get $t = 5$ and gave $t$ instead of the length of $\overline{QR}$.
I matched $PQ$ with $YZ$, so I solved $3t + 4 = 2t + 7$ to get $t = 3$ and then $QR = YZ = 2(3) + 7 = 13$.
I found $t = 5$ correctly but then computed $PQ = 3(5) + 4 = 19$ instead of $QR$.

hints: Corresponding sides of congruent triangles are equal. Which side of $XYZ$ matches $\overline{PQ}$?
$\overline{PQ}$ corresponds to $\overline{XY}$, so $3t + 4 = 5t - 6$. Also $\overline{QR}$ corresponds to $\overline{YZ}$.

solutions.reliable: Since $P \leftrightarrow X$ and $Q \leftrightarrow Y$, side $\overline{PQ}$ corresponds to $\overline{XY}$, so $3t + 4 = 5t - 6$, giving $2t = 10$ and $t = 5$. Side $\overline{QR}$ corresponds to $\overline{YZ}$, so $QR = YZ = 2(5) + 7 = 17$ centimeters. Check: $PQ = XY = 19$.
